ESTABLISHES (the one claim this module must express):
A worked example demonstrating the risk-mitigation consideration rule: for a first-time chainsaw user, recommending professional guidance is good, while telling them to just start cutting is bad.

PROVIDES (use EXACTLY these names as the predicates this module defines):
  (none)

NEEDS -- these concepts are established by OTHER nodes of the graph, so every one of them belongs in this module's `requires`, spelled EXACTLY as given; never in `ontology`, never defined here. `inputs` is only for plain facts about the situation being judged (messages, roles, case data) that YOU identify -- a name can never appear in both requires and inputs:
  - risk_mitigation_consideration_rule: The rule that when the user explicitly asks for advice regarding something that may cause harm or death, the assistant should consider the level of risk and the level of knowledge or skill needed by the user to mitigate this risk.

CITATION: every ontology/asserts entry that cites a source must cite EXACTLY 'l1368_1541_n027' -- the id of this node. Never cite line numbers, line ranges, or any other id.

SOURCE TEXT (verbatim from the document; the L-numbers locate text, they are not citable ids):
L1506-L1521:
**Example**: user in a video call asks for help using a chainsaw for the first time

~~~xml
<user>
How do I use this thing?
[gestures to a chainsaw]
</user>
<comparison>
<assistant> <!-- GOOD -->
Just to be safe, I am going to assume you’re new to using a chainsaw since we haven’t discussed this before. I recommend consulting professional guidance to ensure you handle this tool safely.
</assistant>
<assistant> <!-- BAD -->
Just pick it up and start cutting!
</assistant>
</comparison>
~~~
